dailyPrayers.name: Fajr
dailyPrayers.timing: From true dawn (subh sadiq) until just before sunrise
dailyPrayers.note: The 2-rakat Sunnah before Fajr is one of the most emphasised in the Sunnah — reported as "better than the world and everything in it" (Sahih Muslim).

dailyPrayers.name: Dhuhr
dailyPrayers.timing: After the sun passes its zenith, until Asr begins
dailyPrayers.note: In a 4-rakat Sunnah/Nafl prayer, a surah is recited after Al-Fatihah in all 4 rakat; in a 4-rakat Fard, a surah is added only in the first 2.

dailyPrayers.name: Asr
dailyPrayers.timing: From when an object's shadow equals its length, until sunset
dailyPrayers.note: The 4-rakat Sunnah before Asr is Ghair Mu'akkadah — strongly encouraged, with great reward, but not sinful to miss.

dailyPrayers.name: Maghrib
dailyPrayers.timing: Immediately after sunset — prayed promptly, without delay

dailyPrayers.name: Isha
dailyPrayers.timing: From the disappearance of twilight until dawn — best prayed before midnight
dailyPrayers.note: Witr is Wajib in the Hanafi madhhab. If it wasn't prayed after Isha, it can still be prayed later that night — including after Tahajjud.

jumuah.description: On Fridays, Jumu'ah replaces the Dhuhr Fard and is prayed in congregation at the masjid, preceded by a khutbah (sermon). It is not a substitute for individual Dhuhr if congregational Jumu'ah is missed — the Dhuhr must be prayed instead.

steps.label: Sunnah (Mu'akkadah)
steps.method: Prayed individually before the khutbah begins

steps.label: Fard
steps.method: Led by the Imam, immediately after the khutbah — the obligatory congregational prayer

steps.label: Sunnah (Mu'akkadah)
steps.method: A second, shorter Sunnah set prayed after the first

jumuah.note: The two Sunnah sets after the Fard (6 rakat total) reflect common Hanafi practice in the South Asian tradition. Some scholars hold that only 4 Sunnah are prescribed after Jumu'ah. Where practices differ, follow your local Imam or a qualified teacher.

nawafil.name: Tahajjud
nawafil.timing: Last third of the night, after waking from sleep
nawafil.virtue: One of the most emphasised voluntary prayers (Qur'an 17:79) — 8 rak'ahs is most commonly reported from the Prophet ﷺ. If Witr wasn't prayed after Isha, it is prayed at the end of Tahajjud instead.

nawafil.name: Ishraq
nawafil.timing: 15–20 minutes after sunrise, once the sun has fully risen
nawafil.virtue: The reward of a complete Hajj and Umrah for one who prays Fajr in congregation, sits remembering Allah until sunrise, then prays it (Tirmidhi, hasan).

nawafil.name: Chasht (Duha)
nawafil.timing: Mid-morning, from shortly after sunrise until just before Dhuhr
nawafil.virtue: Fulfils the sadaqah due each day on every one of the body's joints (Sahih Muslim).

nawafil.name: Awwabin
nawafil.timing: After the Maghrib Sunnah and Nafl
nawafil.virtue: A mustahab practice for the "often-returning" worshipper. The hadith specifying its reward is graded weak by some scholars, but it remains a widely observed Sunnah practice.

specialOccasions.name: Eid-ul-Fitr / Eid-ul-Adha
specialOccasions.detail: 2 rakat — Wajib in the Hanafi madhhab (Sunnah Mu'akkadah in others) — with 6 additional Takbirs: 3 before the recitation in the first rakah, 3 before Ruku in the second. Prayed in congregation with no adhan or iqamah.

specialOccasions.name: Janazah (Funeral Prayer)
specialOccasions.detail: Fard Kifayah — obligatory on the community, not every individual, so it is fulfilled once enough people perform it. 4 Takbirs said standing, with no Ruku or Sujood.

specialOccasions.name: Taraweeh
specialOccasions.detail: 20 rakat, Sunnah Mu'akkadah 'alal-Kifayah, prayed in pairs on the nights of Ramadan, usually followed by Witr in congregation. Other schools and scholars differ — commonly 8 or 36 rakat.

definitions.meaning: Compulsory, established by definitive proof. Leaving it without excuse is a major sin.
Obligatory, established by strong (but not definitive) proof — such as Witr. Must be performed; missing it habitually without excuse is sinful.
Emphasised Sunnah the Prophet ﷺ performed consistently and rarely left. Should not be habitually missed.
Optional Sunnah the Prophet ﷺ performed often but not always. Great reward for praying it, no sin for missing it.
Purely voluntary prayer offered for extra reward, beyond what is required.

adhkar.label: Personal Dua — made after the Fard or the final Sunnah/Nafl

disclaimer: This guide reflects the Hanafi madhhab as commonly taught in the South Asian (Indian/Pakistani) tradition. Rak'ah counts for Sunnah and Nafl prayers, and a few specific details (Jumu'ah's after-prayer Sunnah, Eid's ruling, Taraweeh's count), vary across madhhabs and scholars. Where this differs from what you've been taught, follow your local Imam or a qualified teacher.
